title: Iris and the Seed Mystery
markdown:
Twilight painted the garden in soft colours. Iris watched the bird table. The sunflower seeds vanished so fast, even after Professor Elm refilled them. She put her chin on her hand, notebook and pencil ready. “A little puzzle.” First she watched from the window. No birds or squirrels showed their secrets. The seeds simply went.

Button, a gentle badger, ambled over. “What’s troubling you?”

“The bird table. Empty again.”

Professor Elm, the wise old owl, blinked. “Have you tried notes?”

Iris nodded. “When he fills it. When it’s empty.” She showed the pages: dates and times, no clear pattern. So she decided to draw. The table, the fence posts, the clouds. The seed levels again and again, each tiny change with the pencil.

One sunny afternoon, sketching dappled light, she noticed swift movements at the base. Little whiskered fellows, popping from the earth and vanishing in a blink. She scribbled them. When they were near, the seeds dropped faster.

“Someone is taking them.”

Button rumbled. “Where might they be going?”

“Let’s find out.” She marked a few seeds with a tiny dot of berry juice. She and Button waited, breaths soft in the warm air.

The sun dipped, oranges and golds. A small busy family of field mice scurried to the table. Incredible speed. Marked seeds in little paws. Then, like shadows, into a hidden burrow under the old oak.

Iris gasped, wonder without a speech. “Winter stores.”

Elm hooted softly and did not mention tapestries or giving up. She had watched, recorded, marked, followed. Button nodded his big head. Pieces, found.

Iris closed the notebook with a click. The bird table was not only for birds; it was a supply station. She left the last pale stars to arrive without promising dreams. Tomorrow the table would empty again, and she would already know why, which was a different kind of full.
